question: An engineer must ensure fabric redundancy when implementing NPV mode on a Cisco MDS 9000 Series Switch. Which action enables fabric redundancy?
options: Use TE ports to connect to upstream switches.
Add a port channel to upstream switches.
Configure the NPV devices to use an external FLOGI database.
Connect the NPV devices to multiple upstream switches.
theory: An NPV edge switch has no fabric-services intelligence of its own (no domain ID, no local zoning/name-server) - it is entirely dependent on its upstream core switch(es) for fabric membership. To avoid a single point of failure, an NPV edge switch should be connected, via separate NP uplinks, to multiple independent upstream NPIV-enabled core switches so that a failure of one core switch or its uplink doesn't take down every path from the edge devices into the fabric. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 8 - NPIV and NPV)
